thread:
infra-bot: [ALERT] Billing anomaly: GPU spend 2.9x baseline in last 60m for project:redwood-inference-prod. id=trace-ef3
Alex: noticed the alert, looking at cost dashboard — us-west1 shows a sudden compute/GPU spike
Priya: checking autoscaler logs; it tried to resolve reservation 'res-gpu-usw' and couldn't find it, CA fell back to generic instance template
Priya: relevant log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T21:10:02Z autoscaler: scale-up request node-group=gpu-inference-usw desired=10 current=1
2026-03-17T21:10:03Z reservation-lookup: reservation 'res-gpu-usw' not found
2026-03-17T21:10:03Z fallback: launching 9 instances using 'general-template-usw' type=n1-standard-32
```
Dan: that means CPU-only nodes launched in us-west1 — they don't satisfy pod GPU requests but are still billed at on-demand rates
Marta: where are our committed GPU reservations actually located? I thought we had committed capacity in us-central1 for A2-family
Alex: correct, commitments/discounts are for us-central1 (commitment id: cm-2025-a2-uscentral). No matching reservation exists in us-west1
Sam: quick root cause: a terraform rename in infra repo changed the reservation resource name but the zone attribute was not updated, so the reservation never got provisioned in us-west
Sam: quick command to verify: `gcloud compute reservations list --filter="name~gpu" --zones` -> shows only us-central entries
Priya: estimated impact so far: ~38 GPU-equivalent hours charged at on-demand plus extra CPU instance hours. Ballpark $9.8k excess in last 3 hours
Alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale down the fallback IG to 0; 2) revoke MIG/quota in us-west temporarily to block new launches; 3) either create reservation or disable autoscaler in that region
Priya: applied a terraform patch to create reservation + necessary labels; forcing reservation creation (ETA ~25m). Patch snippet:
```
resource "google_compute_reservation" "gpu_reservation_usw" {
  name = "res-gpu-usw"
  zone = "us-west1-b"
  specific_reservation { /* GPU shape config */ }
  labels = { "inference" = "gpu" }
}
```
Dan: running a BigQuery billing export query to enumerate non-us-central GPU hours and which service accounts/owners triggered instance creation (I'll post results)
Marta: also capture which deploys touched instance template naming — this looks like naming drift; we need a git-backed guardrail
Sam: short-term fix: I'll add a CI check that verifies instance template labels and reservation mapping against autoscaler discovery rules. PR inbound (ETA 1d)
Priya: resized fallback IG: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize general-template-usw --size 0 --zone us-west1-b`
infra-bot: [INFO] Instance group general-template-usw resized to 0 at 2026-03-17T21:33:47Z
Alex: after scale-down and no new launches, projected excess spend drops to ~$1.1k for the day
Marta: action items recap:
- Alex: own postmortem + runbook update (map region -> reservation id, include preflight checks)
- Sam: add CI guard for naming/labels (ETA 1d)
- Priya: add terraform preflight to validate reservation existence before apply (ETA 2d)
- Dan: finish billing query to attribute owners and attach evidence (ETA 45m)
Priya: opening incident ticket IN-7891 with root cause: terraform rename drift -> reservation missing in region -> autoscaler fallback -> on-demand launches. Attaching cost calc + mitigation steps
Alex: good work. let's add a deploy gate that validates reservation coverage for any GPU-capable node-group. keep updates in this thread until the postmortem is complete :thumbsup:
